sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

stage_1.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / certificate of good standing (certificado de vigencia) of each foreign corporate shareholder
stage_1.issuing_entity: Competent company register of the shareholder's country of origin
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) followed by sworn Spanish translation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated Spanish Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC); arts. 4-10 (types and legal personality), 20-23 (incorporation requirements), 22 (minimum SL capital EUR 3,000), 33 (legal personality acquired only upon registration), 62-63 and 76 (fully paid-up cash contributions), 133-138 (management body), 209-215 (single administrator and board); supplemented by Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Mercantile Registry Regulations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid) for deed inscription; under the supervisory coordination of the Ministerio de Justicia and the Colegio de Registradores de España.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation together with the statutory bylaws) granted before a Spanish notary and filed for registration at the Provincial Mercantile Registry; the incorporation is then published in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL minimum share capital is EUR 3,000 (art. 22 LSC), fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash at formation (art. 76 LSC). The cash amount must be deposited in a Spanish bank account opened in the name of the company in formation or delivered to the notary in blocked custody; the bank certificate (certificado bancario de desembolso) or notarial deposit receipt serves as the escrow evidence and the funds cannot be withdrawn before registry inscription. The bylaws may fix a higher statutory capital; any later reduction below EUR 3,000 is prohibited.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the inaugural organizational meeting of the founding members duly convened on [date]: 1. That the entire initial share capital of EUR 3,000 be subscribed and fully paid in cash, and that 3,000 quota-participations be allotted as set out in the incorporation deed. 2. That the registered office of the company be established at [street address], Madrid, Spain, and that all filings with the Registro Mercantil de Madrid be authorized. 3. That [full name] be appointed Sole Administrator, accepting office, with the powers conferred under Article 234 of the Spanish Capital Companies Act. 4. That the corporate object of designing, developing and publishing hyper-casual mobile games and ad-monetization (ISIC 5820) commence forthwith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Madrid - online portal www.rmc.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application naming up to three proposed SL names, each including the suffix Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada or SL. The RMC searches against existing and reserved names and, if no identical or confusingly similar name exists, issues a negative name certificate valid for three months. The certificate must be produced to the notary and to the Provincial Mercantile Registry at filing. Download the certified PDF or request the original certificate by mail.
required_dossiers: Passport, DNI or NIE of each founding member
Proposed company names (at least two alternatives)
Online RMC application form specifying the SL type and the intended activity (CNAE 2009 code 5820 optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RMC returns a coincidence or refusal, file a rectification request setting out arguments against the conflicting entry, submit new alternative names, or appeal to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) where the negative certificate is alleged to be unjustified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the Formation Bank Account and Depositing Share Capital (Desembolso del Capital)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution chosen by the founders (commercial banking unit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the full EUR 3,000 share capital. Obtain a bank certificate (certificado bancario de desembolso) showing the account holder, account number, deposit date and balance, and stating that the funds are blocked until the company is registered. Deliver this certificate to the notary for inclusion in the deed. The bank will apply standard KYC/AML due diligence; the business is classified low-risk for gaming software publishing.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all founding members and account signatories
Name reservation certificate issued by the RMC
Draft corporate object and structure summary for the bank KYC/AML review
Provisional NIF application form, when already filed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the KYC documentation, provide the corporate project, proof of residential address, and a source-of-funds declaration. In case of refusal, select another Spanish credit institution, update the documentation, and reopen the account without loss of the name certificate validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Delegación de Grandes Empresas or local tax office; online at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Modelo 036 (census registration) marked as solicitud de NIF provisional together with the name certificate and the draft deed or a descriptive memorandum of the company. The AEAT issues the provisional NIF beginning with the letter B for an SL. The provisional NIF must be quoted in the notarial deed and is later converted to the definitive NIF after registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of negative name from the RMC
Project of the deed or draft bylaws
Identity documents of the proposed administrator or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT requires corrections or rejects the submission, amend and resubmit Modelo 036 electronically or in person; if issuance is not made within the legal deadline, file a jurisdictional claim or request urgent handling at the local delegation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Granting of the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary (Notaría) chosen by the founders within the territorial Notarial College of the registered office, normally Colegio Notarial de Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend before the notary with the bank certificate, name certificate, provisional NIF and identity documents of all founders. The notary verifies capacity, licenses none required for the software activity, and reads the bylaws including the object clause covering development and publishing of hyper-casual mobile games, online advertising and ad-monetization. All founders sign the deed, the notary issues the original first copy and authorised second copy, and the notary electronically forwards the deed to the tax office and the Mercantile Registry where required.
required_dossiers: Certificado bancario de desembolso evidencing the EUR 3,000 deposit
Draft statutes (estatutos sociales) prepared by counsel or the notary
Passport, DNI or NIE of every founding member and every appointed administrator
Evidence of payment of the notarial fee (arancel notarial) and the dispatch or payment instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects defects (insufficient deposit, identity mismatch, lack of representative capacity or invalid clause), cure the defect by completing the bank deposit, providing a properly notarised power of attorney, or granting an additional corrective deed before the same notary before re-signature.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and official portal at https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF automatically upon incorporation with Registro Mercantil. Non-resident owners must appoint a Spanish tax representative and file Form 036 or equivalent online application to AEAT for NIF and VAT identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election available. Hybrid mismatch and ATAD rules govern cross-border structures; tax residency can be elected via specific AEAT procedures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing via Facturae standard or AEAT digital stamps (sello electrónico) for all VAT returns and B2B transactions; real-time filing and clearance through the AEAT portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT applies to goods physically exported outside the EU or services supplied to non-taxable persons outside Spain, provided export is proven and goods/services are not consumed in Spain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger penalties of up to 100% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback and loss of refund rights upon audit if documentation is inadequate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) - competent AML/CFT supervisor for credit institutions, EMIs, and payment institutions, and administrator of the SDO (Sistema de Declaración de Operaciones) statistical reporting portal. Foreign exchange, trade, and foreign investment policy is coordinated by the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones under the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account operations. Spain, as a euro-area Member State, applies TFEU Articles 63-65 on free movement of capital; no exchange-control authorisation, FX surrender mechanism, or repatriation permit is required. Ad-network revenue remittance, shareholder loans, and dividend distributions are unrestricted. Dividend/interest/royalty payments to non-residents are subject to 19% withholding tax (treaty relief available). Two reporting thresholds apply: (i) cash or bearer-means movements at or above EUR 10,000 must be declared to customs/authorities, and (ii) payments/collections with non-residents at or above EUR 50,000 per transaction require a balance-of-payments statistical declaration through the bank intermediary (or directly via the SDO portal). There are no restrictions on holding foreign-currency accounts in Spain.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil. Spain imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export or service proceeds. EUR and foreign-currency accounts may be freely held. For hyper-casual game publishers (ISIC 5820), inbound AdMob/AppLovin proceeds are treated as exports of services; the only compliance obligation is the SDO statistical declaration for collections from non-residents at or above EUR 50,000, plus retention of publisher contracts, payout statements, and invoicing records for audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit and Operational Treasury Account (certificado de depósito for capital injection; EUR current account with USD sub-account; SWIFT BIC BSCHESMM)
Cuenta Vista Empresas (operational EUR/USD accounts; SWIFT BIC BBVAESMM; automatic SDO filing and FX forward lines)
Cuenta de Negocio (operational treasury and FX hedging desk; SWIFT BIC CAIXESBB; strong cash-pooling for LATAM flows)
BStartup/Expansión Company Account (EUR; digital onboarding with video identification; SWIFT BIC BSABESBB)
Cuenta Empresa (EUR and foreign-currency accounts; remote opening with electronic signature; SWIFT BIC BKBKESMM)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operating collections; Low for capital escrow and primary clearing. EMIs/payment institutions passporting into Spain or operating under an EEA home-state licence (e.g., Payoneer, Wise Business, Currencycloud, MangoPay) may receive AdMob/AppLovin USD/EUR payouts and convert funds; however, they are not credit institutions, do not benefit from the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund, and their IBANs may trigger source-of-funds escalation at Spanish tier-1 banks. AdMob/AppLovin payout verification via publisher console is the essential mitigation. The SL should maintain a domestic tier-1 account as the single treasury spine and use EMIs only for secondary collection currencies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid model. Fully remote onboarding is feasible for SLs whose directors, apoderados, and UBOs (above 25%) hold a Spanish NIE and electronic certificate (Sabadell, Bankinter, BBVA video-ident), but the majority of tier-1 banks require one in-branch meeting for at least one Spanish resident director, or a notarised power of attorney with Apostille/legalisation appointing a local KYC representative. The bank will also require the standard AML questionnaire (form S22), the UBO/titular real declaration, and a source-of-wealth statement for any non-resident shareholder contributing capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident founder injecting equity via personal funds without clear source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital increase or shareholder loan deed; SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation from the origin bank; six months of origin bank statements; tax residence certificate; signed source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration; founder's professional track record and prior company documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ad-network inflows (AdMob/AppLovin) arriving in high volume immediately after incorporation, inconsistent with declared operational history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Google AdMob Publisher Terms and AppLovin Publishing Agreement; monthly payout statements and revenue reports from both networks; Google Play Console and Apple App Store Connect dashboards; app metadata and launch dates; independent mediation agreements (ironSource, Unity Ads).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual substance - shared registered office, no payroll records, IP held offshore, and no verifiable local activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Office lease or registered-address service invoice; Seguridad Social (RETA/TCR) registration and employment contracts; VAT/Modelo 303 filings showing reverse-charge advertising input VAT; monthly accounting pack and audit-ready financials; bank access to live dashboards evidencing user-acquisition spend.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments routed through unregulated ad-tech intermediaries or mixing trade and intercompany royalty flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Whitelisted counterparty register with full KYC packs for Meta, TikTok, Google, Apple, and mediation platforms; invoice-to-wire matching evidence; transfer pricing documentation for intercompany royalties/service fees; origin-and-destination bank reference letters; purpose codes consistent with ISIC 5820 and ISIC 7310 (advertising).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 (non-EEA) or SEPA Credit Transfer (EEA) to the SL's Spanish IBAN (prefix ES + 22 digits, BIC of receiving bank, e.g., BSCHESMM Santander). Remittance purpose must be explicitly coded: 'Aportación de capital social / Ampliación de capital - Art. 62 de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital' for equity, or 'Préstamo de socios / operación vinculada' for shareholder loans. No prior FX authorisation is required; the receiving bank automatically files the SDO balance-of-payments declaration when the transaction equals or exceeds EUR 50,000. Post-receipt obligations: formalise the capital increase or loan in a notarial deed, register it at the Registro Mercantil, update the shareholder book, file the FDI ex-post declaration (Modelo D-1A via the electronic registry of the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones) where thresholds are met, including newly created companies; file Modelo 232 for related-party transactions above EUR 250,000 per counterparty; maintain market-rate interest documentation for shareholder loans. FDI screening under Ley 8/2020 is not applicable to game publishing unless the investor is state-owned or the target falls within a critical sector (not applicable here).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Two primary rails: SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant for EEA payees (ad servers, EU service providers) and SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA counterparties (e.g., TikTok Pte. Ltd. (Singapore), Apple Distribution International (Ireland), LATAM media buyers). Each outgoing wire must cite the underlying invoice and reference 'servicios publicitarios y promoción' with the correct SDO classifier; payments at or above EUR 50,000 trigger automatic Banco de España reporting. For hyper-casual publishing, commercial letters of credit are not standard; standby LCs (SBLC) may collateralise IP-licensing obligations in co-publishing agreements and must comply with UCP600/ISBP and the bank's documentary acceptance rules (presentation drafts, invoices, confirmatory certificates). All UA, platform fee, and revenue share disbursements should flow from the same central treasury account with sub-ledger automation to preserve clean audit trails for tax, AML, and balance-of-payments purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward (Compraventa de Divisas a Plazo) on EUR/USD, executed against documented monthly AdMob/AppLovin USD receivables
FX Swap (Swap de Divisas) covering EUR/USD period mismatches between USD inflows and EUR-denominated UA expenses
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) for intercompany/shareholder loans where principal and interest legs are swapped EUR/USD

FX Option and zero-premium Collar structures (MiFID II appropriateness and proportionality tests apply for an SL classified as retail client unless it opts up to professional or eligible counterparty status)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) for LATAM risk operations (ARS, BRL, MXN, COP) where the SL acts as a European treasury bridge, subject to counterparty ISDA/NDF master confirmation and internal treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval of the annual accounts by the General Meeting of Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 3,000 EUR and potential dissolution proceedings if not remedied

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Net turnover exceeding 7 million EUR, total assets exceeding 3.5 million EUR, or more than 50 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) or IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update of the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) for shareholding transfers and changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general rate for Spanish-resident companies. Qualifying newly created entities generally apply 15% in the first tax period with a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the 15% new-entity rate, research and development and technological innovation credits, and qualifying patent-box relief. Eligibility, caps, documentation, and recapture rules apply. Spain's reduced rates for microenterprises are subject to turnover, taxable-base, and phased-in-year rules and should be confirmed for the relevant tax year.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite; Spanish tax losses do not have a fixed expiry period. Utilization is generally capped at 70% of the pre-loss taxable base, subject to a EUR 1 million minimum deduction and statutory company-size and restructuring rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) e-office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the ordinary deadline is 25 July of the following year, subject to official deadline extensions or non-business-day rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company's Spanish tax identification number (NIF), legal name, tax period, registered address, and applicable entity and regime codes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An SL is Spanish tax-resident by incorporation under Spanish law. Foreign ownership does not convert it into a non-resident taxpayer; report the SL's own NIF and tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile the financial-accounting result to the Spanish tax base, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation adjustments, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SL's worldwide income, subject to applicable treaty relief, foreign-tax credits, and Spanish tax rules. Do not report the shareholder's income as the SL's income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable base after applicable adjustments and deductions for prior-period tax losses, within statutory utilization limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same loss-utilization rules to the Spanish-resident SL regardless of shareholder residence; maintain evidence supporting the losses and ownership continuity where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate, credits, and final tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the rate applicable to the entity and tax period; claim eligible credits and incentives with supporting records; calculate the final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim incentives only where the SL satisfies Spanish statutory conditions. Foreign tax credits require qualifying foreign tax, income attribution, and supporting proof.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholdings, payments on account, and settlement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit Spanish withholdings and instalment payments (including Modelo 202 payments) and determine the balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile payments made under the SL's NIF. A non-resident shareholder's withholding on a later distribution is not a credit of the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable related-party, deduction, incentive, and other supplementary schedules and retain required supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border related-party transactions and apply Spanish transfer-pricing rules regardless of the counterparty's residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior tax-authority request is generally subject to the voluntary late-filing surcharge under General Tax Law Article 27: 1% plus 1% for each full month of delay; after 12 months, generally 15% plus late-payment interest. If a return is filed after a request or tax adjustment, tax penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on the infringement and aggravating factors. Late payment has separate surcharge rules. Additional fixed penalties may apply to information-reporting failures. Current statutory reductions and procedural rules should be checked for the filing year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax instalment-payment return, filed electronically through the AEAT e-office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalment payments, generally in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1–20 April, 1–20 October, and 1–20 December; the applicable statutory or AEAT calendar adjustment applies where the final day is a non-business day. Payment method may affect the effective payment deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's NIF, tax period, and relevant instalment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish-resident SL's NIF; foreign shareholders do not file this return for the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Instalment calculation basis and applicable method
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the instalment using the method selected or required under Spanish law: generally a percentage of the prior-period tax liability, or, where applicable or elected, a percentage of the current-period taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the SL's legally applicable method and include Spanish-taxable results of the SL; do not substitute the shareholder's residence-country tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct qualifying prior instalments and calculate the payment due for the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only payments and credits attributable to the SL and support the figures with its accounting and tax records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing instalment payments may trigger statutory surcharges and late-payment interest; failure to file or underpayment following a tax-authority request may also result in tax penalties. The amount depends on the delay, tax due, conduct, and applicable voluntary-correction rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% generally applies to dividends paid by a Spanish company to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. A qualifying EU parent may obtain an exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Spanish implementing law, subject to minimum holding, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and other conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the Spanish payer with a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the competent foreign tax authority, together with evidence of beneficial ownership and satisfaction of the relevant treaty or EU-law conditions. The payer generally applies the domestic rate unless it has sufficient documentation to apply relief at source. Where excess withholding is made, the recipient may claim a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident refund procedure and forms. Treaty eligibility and documentation requirements depend on the recipient's residence and the specific treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish non-resident withholding rate is 19% on Spanish-source interest and royalties, subject to exemptions and treaty reductions. Interest and qualifying royalties paid to an associated company in another EU Member State may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, subject to qualifying relationship, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse, and other conditions. Applicable treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and income classification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: There is no single transaction-value threshold that universally triggers both a Local File and Master File. Related-party transactions must be arm's length. Documentation exemptions and simplified documentation may apply, including for qualifying entities with net turnover below EUR 45 million, subject to exclusions and transaction-specific rules. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Confirm the applicable tax-year thresholds and Spanish implementing rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a general offshore Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to that of certain low-tax jurisdictions. Spanish tax residence, permanent-establishment, transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and substance-over-form rules remain relevant. The SL should maintain genuine decision-making, personnel, premises, accounting, and operational evidence appropriate to its activities and risk profile.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, fabricating expenses, omitting material income, using false invoices, or knowingly filing materially inaccurate returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the tax improperly avoided, depending on the infringement and aggravating factors; serious tax fraud may also constitute a criminal offense. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and period may meet the basic criminal threshold under the Spanish Criminal Code, subject to statutory elements and exceptions; aggravated cases carry higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal fines, disqualification, and imprisonment where they personally participate in or direct tax fraud. Civil or tax liability may attach under statutory responsibility rules where their conduct or failure to act satisfies the legal test. Corporate status does not automatically shield a culpable director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party services, intellectual property, financing, or advertising arrangements outside arm's length without defensible analysis, or failing to maintain required records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make primary and consequential adjustments, assess tax and interest, and impose specific transfer-pricing documentation penalties or general tax penalties depending on the facts, the documentation failure, and the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability for intentional or grossly negligent participation, or under statutory subsidiary-liability rules where their conduct satisfies the legal requirements. A pricing adjustment alone does not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared or improperly withheld cross-border distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties without withholding or reporting required amounts, or applying treaty or EU relief without substantiating eligibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be liable for unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties. Relief-at-source claims unsupported by valid residence and beneficial-ownership evidence may be denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face statutory tax-liability consequences for culpable failure to withhold or remit, and criminal exposure for deliberate fraud. Liability depends on statutory conditions and individual conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fictitious residence, permanent-establishment, or substance arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal foreign entity or sham contractual structure to conceal where the business is effectively managed, where personnel perform functions, or where income-generating activity occurs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may recharacterize the arrangement, determine Spanish residence or a Spanish permanent establishment, assess tax, interest, and penalties, and deny treaty or exemption benefits under domestic anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal exposure may arise for directors who knowingly implement or conceal the arrangement, including tax-crime liability where criminal thresholds and elements are met. A shell-company finding alone does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and illicit payment flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly processing proceeds of crime, disguising payment beneficiaries, or structuring transfers to conceal the origin or destination of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish anti-money-laundering and criminal laws may impose substantial fines, business restrictions, asset confiscation, and imprisonment, depending on the offense and the person's role.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who participate in, authorize, or knowingly facilitate laundering may face personal criminal liability, fines, disqualification, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax sanction and require a separate legal basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commingling company and personal assets, distributing assets unlawfully, or using the SL to defraud creditors or evade legal obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include repayment, insolvency-related liability, administrative or criminal sanctions, and disregard of limited liability in exceptional cases under applicable law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for damage caused by breach of duties and, in insolvency, statutory liability where the legal conditions are met. Veil piercing, civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment are not automatic consequences of ordinary tax non-compliance.
